{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study quantifies the agreement between animal model toxicities and human clinical toxicities using metrics like positive predictive values (PPV), negative predictive values (NPV), kappa statistics, balanced accuracy rate (BAR), and Matthew's correlation coefficient (MCC). It explicitly compares preclinical animal results to human clinical outcomes for oncology drugs.",
  "arm": "toxicology",
  "arm_evidence": "Our goal was to determine through a meta-analysis whether the current method of conducting preclinical analysis of toxicities in animals accurately predicts the toxicities of the new wave of targeted oncology drugs.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "oncology"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study focuses on predicting toxicities seen in Phase 1 clinical trials of oncology drugs.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "A total of 90 drugs (83% of drugs) had data available for rats, 77 (71%) for dogs, 40 (37%) for monkeys and 28 (26%) for mice.",
  "species": [
    "rat",
    "dog",
    "non-human-primate",
    "mouse"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "A total of 90 drugs (83% of drugs) had data available for rats, 77 (71%) for dogs, 40 (37%) for monkeys and 28 (26%) for mice.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "For both preclinical and clinical data, toxicities were assessed according to the categories and not the specific toxicities (e.g., either a seizure or a headache would indicate that a drug has neurologic/psychiatric toxicities). For clinical data, grade 3 or 4 toxicities were noted during data collection."
